correctness.rationale: The two disjoint classes of connected induced subsets give a complete signed expansion. The four local sign states reduce each character to 4j−m±3^j with proved exact multiplicity; the zero equation and monotone gap bound hold for all m>=2. An independent adjacency-based subset enumeration and integer fast Walsh transform match for m=1..8, including m=7 nullity 5103 and gap 6. Parseval and Fourier sum identities were checked. Finite runs are supplemental to the all-orders elementary proof.

value.rationale: Balanced spiders are a classical natural extremal family for connected-subtree counting. The theorem gives an exact all-orders closed Fourier spectrum, sparse exponential singularity pattern, exact kernel sizes, and sharp nonzero deconvolution gaps. Even unsigned counts fail to decide Fourier invertibility (m=3 and m=5 have even connected-subtree totals but no Walsh zeros), so the results are not merely reformulations of known unsigned enumeration or routine finite tabulation. No downstream theorem is required for its structural Fourier-recovery utility.
